title: How to Read an Insurance Policy: The 6-Step Practical Guide
description: A step-by-step roadmap to deciphering policy legalese. Learn how to dissect the Declarations Page, read exclusions, identify conditions, and spot coverage traps.
author: David Sterling

content.text: Most people never open their insurance policy envelope until disaster strikes—and by then, discovering an unexpected exclusion or sub-limit is too late. Reading an insurance policy does not require a law degree if you follow this structured 6-step roadmap.

items: Step 1: Scrutinize the Declarations Page: Verify your name spelling, property address, coverage limits, policy effective dates, and deductible amounts.
Step 2: Check the Definitions Section: Note bolded or italicized terms in the text. Insurers define words like 'dwelling', 'motor vehicle', or 'occurrence' with narrow legal meanings.
Step 3: Read the Insuring Agreement: Find the carrier's core promise to see whether you have a 'Named Peril' or 'Open Perils' policy.
Step 4: Audit Section I & II Exclusions: Check what is NOT covered. On home policies, look for flood, earthquake, mold, and sewer backup exclusions.
Step 5: Review Policy Conditions: Understand your duties after a loss, reporting deadlines, and how claim depreciation is calculated (Replacement Cost vs Actual Cash Value).
Step 6: Inspect Attached Endorsements: Verify that any add-on endorsements you paid for (such as scheduled jewelry or water backup) are physically attached to the jacket.

items.question: What does 'Replacement Cost' vs 'Actual Cash Value' mean in property policies?
items.answer: Replacement Cost pays to buy a brand new equivalent item at today's retail prices. Actual Cash Value (ACV) deducts depreciation for age and wear, leaving you with significantly less money.

content.text: Policy forms follow standardized ISO or proprietary bureau templates. Consult your agent for contract clarifications.
